correctness.rationale: For a periodic lower mechanical word the prefix and suffix counts telescope to the forward and backward length-ell increments at s. With j=sb mod n and r=ell*b mod n, they are floor(ell*b/n)+1_{j+r>=n} and floor(ell*b/n)+1_{r>j}. Equality yields the two closed/open residue ranges as given, also for overlapping windows. Each range has min(j,n-1-j) residues and coprimality gives bijections in both length and rotation. The multiplicities, including n=2 and the unique odd-length all-border rotation, follow. The frozen finite checker is consistent with these definitions; the unrestricted claim follows from the proof.
residual_risks: The result is restricted to the coprime labeled binary setting; overlap is allowed.

evidence: Lexicographic row i is rotation by i*q^{-1} mod n of the lower word, with q=b and p=n-b. In the one-part partition of a prefix of length m the height increases by one at the single transition i=m*p mod n, specified by equation (1) and the end-of-prefix exchange in the proof.
broader_coverage.reasoning: This gives the row-resolved prefix height for every proper m, not just the multiset of heights. The known result stated for p>q covers b>n/2 as well by relabeling symbols, which reverses the row order, sending j to n-1-j and r to n-r. These reflections preserve the border criterion and counts. The only equal-count coprime case n=2 is immediate.
searches: arXiv:1804.08724 Lemma 1, proof of Theorem 1, §1.4 equation (1) and Corollary 1

evidence: Write F_m(j) for prefix height in lexicographic row j. The one-part formula gives F_m(j)=F_m(0)+1_{j>=mp mod n}. For m=ell and m=n-ell the thresholds are n-r and r. The suffix has height b-F_{n-ell}(j), also when it overlaps the prefix. Since the lower row has F_ell(0)+F_{n-ell}(0)=b-1, prefix minus suffix equals -1+1_{j>=n-r}+1_{j>=r}.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Thus a border occurs exactly when one threshold has been crossed, equivalently min(r,n-r)<=j<max(r,n-r). For fixed j this is precisely the frozen two-interval residue union, and counting the two intervals gives the frozen histogram. No additional correlation theorem is needed: both already-known step functions use the same row index.
searches: arXiv:1804.08724 PDF pp. 5–8: row rotations, end-of-prefix exchange, equation (1)

originality.rationale: The claimed paired-window spectrum is a direct corollary of the previously published phase-indexed Christoffel prefix partition, although no separate statement of this exact border spectrum was found. Carey and Clampitt give more than an aggregate factor histogram: their proof specifies the precise row of every height change, and their one-part specialization applies at both complementary lengths. It determines all the claimed values by the following substitution.
residual_risks: This is a statement-level implication, not an assertion that the same border formula was explicitly printed or about the earliest priority of its ingredients.

value.rationale: The invariant is natural and the short direct proof is useful exposition, but for this narrow exact claim the spectrum follows mechanically by taking the two complementary prefix coordinates of a known row partition. The resulting cardinalities and extremal cases are just counts of the two residue intervals. No additional independent phenomenon survives that comparison.
residual_risks: This rejects the frozen spectrum as an independent new result, not its use as an illustrative corollary.
